# `/spec-write` Tracker Mode Flow

> See `docs/layout-reference.md` — canonical authority on FR file shape (per-FR file path, AC-prefix derivation, `## Acceptance Criteria` section).

Detailed tracker-mode procedures for `/spec-write`. Pointed at from
`skills/spec-write/SKILL.md` step 0 to keep the skill under NFR-1.

In `mode: none`, this document is unused.

## Tracker ID Assignment Order

**Rule:** create the tracker ticket **first**, read the returned ID, substitute the placeholder globally, **then** write the FR file. **Never guess** the next sequential tracker number.

The order is load-bearing. Trackers skip cancelled numbers, renumber across workspace renames, and allocate IDs atomically on ticket creation — an implementer's guess ("`<TKR>-NN` was last, so the next is `<TKR>-NN+1`") can be wrong silently, and the misalignment ships into every downstream artifact (AC prefixes, filename, plan-file row, every prose cross-reference).

### Concrete flow

1. **Draft with placeholder.** Use `<tracker-id>` (or adapter-specific rendering — `STE-<N>` for Linear, `PROJ-<N>` for Jira) throughout the draft:
   - AC lines: `AC-<tracker-id>.1`, `AC-<tracker-id>.2`, …
   - Filename: `<tracker-id>.md`
   - Plan-file table row: `| <tracker-id> | Title | <tracker>:<tracker-id> |`
   - Prose cross-references: `"closes <tracker-id>"`, `"supersedes <tracker-id>"`
2. **Create the tracker ticket.** Call `Provider.sync(spec)` → `upsertTicketMetadata(null, …)`. **Workspace binding.** Before invoking, call `readWorkspaceBinding(claudeMdPath, "linear" | "jira")` from `adapters/_shared/src/workspace_binding.ts` and pass `team` + `project` + `defaultLabels` into the call so the new ticket lands on the correct project board with the configured labels. Linear adapter rejects creates that lack `project` per the silent-landing trap; Jira adapter rejects creates that lack `project` per the Jira API requirement. **Labels** are optional and forwarded only when `defaultLabels` is populated (Linear → `save_issue.labels`; Jira → `createJiraIssue.additional_fields.labels`). The tracker allocator returns the real ID (e.g., `<TKR>-NN`).
3. **Substitute globally.** Replace every `<tracker-id>` with the returned ID in one pass.
4. **Write the FR file.** Only after substitution completes — the file on disk never contains a placeholder.

### Worked example

Draft AC line: `AC-<tracker-id>.1: releaseLock asserts pre-state in_progress`

Linear assigns the next free ID (let's call it `<TKR>-NN`) on save.

Final AC line in file: `AC-<TKR>-NN.1: releaseLock asserts pre-state in_progress`
Filename: `specs/frs/<TKR>-NN.md`
Plan row: `| <TKR>-NN | Hide full 26-char ULIDs | linear:<TKR>-NN |`

### Mode: none exemption

Mode: none projects mint the short-ULID tail locally (collision-proof by Crockford Base32 randomness + scan). No tracker allocator, no race. The placeholder rule is tracker-mode only.

## Post-save behavior (tracker mode)

After each AC-list save in `specs/frs/<tracker-id>.md`'s
`## Acceptance Criteria` section:

1. Resolve the ticket-id for the edited FR directly from the filename
   (`<tracker-id>.md`) — the filename IS the binding, no separate
   traceability matrix is consulted. If the FR is brand-new and the
   filename still carries the `<tracker-id>` placeholder, prompt the
   user for a fresh `upsert_ticket_metadata(null, ...)` invocation that
   creates the ticket and substitutes the returned ID per the
   placeholder rule above.
2. Run ticket-binding confirmation per `docs/ticket-binding.md`.
3. Call `pull_acs(ticket_id)` — fresh fetch, just like `/implement` does.
4. Classify the local AC list vs the tracker AC list via the bidirectional
   diff classifier (`adapters/_shared/src/classify_diff.ts`). Full procedure
   in `docs/ac-sync.md`.
5. If any AC is non-`identical`, surface the Schema K diff and run the
   per-AC prompt loop. **Cancel aborts the save** — local changes revert
   to the in-memory draft state (the user re-decides).
6. On resolution (including `all identical` fast path), call
   `upsert_ticket_metadata(ticket_id, title, <rebuilt description>)` to
   push the converged state to the tracker.
   `git log` captures the sync event via the commit; no separate audit
   trail is written.

`/spec-write` on a brand-new FR (no ticket bound yet) skips steps 1–5 and
goes straight to `upsert_ticket_metadata(null, title, description)` to
mint a new ticket; the returned ID becomes the FR filename
(`specs/frs/<tracker-id>.md`) — the filename IS the binding (no
separate traceability matrix is maintained).

## Cancel semantics

- **During diff/resolve cancel (step 5):** local draft stays in memory;
  tracker untouched. User can retry or abandon.
- **During mint-new cancel:** no `upsert_ticket_metadata` call; no FR
  file is written to disk (the draft stays in memory — cancel here means
  "don't push to tracker, don't land the file yet").

## Orphan listing

`/spec-write` § 0.5 never improvises the tracker-orphan list. Fetch the
container with the adapter's `list_active_frs` read (see `adapters/jira.md`
and `adapters/linear.md`), save every page verbatim as a JSON file, then run:

```bash
bun run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/adapters/_shared/src/container_ownership.ts list <projectRoot> <page.json>...
```

Page fields the listing needs:

- **Jira** (`searchJiraIssuesUsingJql`, paginated to `isLast: true`): `key`,
  `summary`, `issuetype`, `labels`, `description`, `creator`, `project`.
- **Linear** (`list_issues`, cursor followed to `hasNextPage: false`):
  `id` / `identifier`, `title`, `labels`, `description`, `createdBy`,
  `project`, `team`.

A repository that declares a shared tracker refuses a page whose ticket lacks
`labels` or `description`, naming the file or the key; a missing or non-JSON
page file refuses too, and nothing is listed from a page that failed to parse.

The listing prints one table row per unbound ticket — `Key`, `Class`, `Owner`
(the creator), `Toolkit-written` (the `Source: specs/frs/<key>.md` back-link,
reported only; it is not ownership evidence) and `Title` — then a `summary:`
line counting every class, the excluded ones included. Classes: `ours` (carries
this repository's `repo_tag`), `unowned` (no owner label — hand-filed, or a
client too old to tag), `sibling` (another repository's label) and `container`
(a Jira Epic or any hierarchy level above the FR). `sibling` and `container`
tickets are counted and never offered. Each offerable ticket gets one line
carrying the two option labels to show verbatim:

```
options: Import <KEY> | Skip <KEY>
```

On an explicit `Import <KEY>` answer, record consent before the import:

```bash
bun run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/adapters/_shared/src/container_ownership.ts consent <projectRoot> <KEY> <page.json>...
```

`consent` re-classifies the same pages and, in a shared repository, writes an
`import` receipt for an `ours` or `unowned` key only; it refuses a `sibling`,
`container` or unlisted key with nothing written. An undeclared repository
writes no receipt.

Then hand the same saved pages to the import as its ownership context,
`importFromTracker(trackerKey, trackerId, provider, specsDir, promptMilestone,
{ projectRoot, pages })`. With the pages, a `sibling` or `container` key
refuses before any write. Importing an `unowned` ticket claims it: the sync
adds this repository's tag to the labels the page shows, so the sibling's next
listing classifies it `sibling`. In a shared repository, a page that lacks the
ticket or its `labels` refuses rather than risk a label set that drops a
label. Where the tag write never lands, probe #49's `bound-ticket-untagged`
row names the ticket.

## MCP call budget (NFR-8)

Per FR save: at most **1** MCP call (`upsert_ticket_metadata`, ≤ 1 per
spec). The additional `pull_acs` in step 3 is shared with the same skill's
pre-flight work and counts toward the 2-call `/implement` budget in
sessions where `/spec-write` chains into `/implement`.

284	
285	1. If `ticket_id_or_null === null`:
286	   - Resolve the issue type: default `Task`, override via
287	     `jira_issue_type:` in the `### Jira` block under `## Task Tracking`.
288	     Default-team-managed Kanban templates have `Task` / `Epic` /
289	     `Subtask` only (no `Story`); `Task` is the universally available
290	     choice. Operators on Scrum templates can switch to `Story` via the
291	     override.
292	   - **Pre-create JQL idempotency probe (single-shot fast path).** Before the
293	     create call fires, look for a ticket this FR already minted on a prior
294	     run (resume / retry) and return that id without writing.
295	
296	     **The decision is a command, not prose.** Run these four steps in order,
297	     with the milestone container flag (`--parent <EpicKey>` for an
298	     Epic-keyed milestone, `--milestone-label <label>` for a grandfathered
299	     numeric one) passed identically to both commands:
300	
301	     1. `bun run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/adapters/_shared/src/create_idempotency_probe.ts query <projectRoot> --title <title> [container]`
302	        — prints ONE JSON line `{ "jql": …, "fields": [...] }`. It reads
303	        `### Jira`.`repo_tag` (a free-form sub-section field, parsed like
304	        `default_labels`) from the binding itself (no tag is ever passed
305	        by hand) and refuses, non-zero, a tag the create would not forward.
306	     2. `mcp__atlassian__searchJiraIssuesUsingJql` with exactly that `jql`
307	        and those `fields` — no edits to either.
308	     3. Save every returned page verbatim as a JSON file (each page after the first with its `requestCursor`, the cursor it was fetched with), then
309	        `bun run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/adapters/_shared/src/create_idempotency_probe.ts decide <projectRoot> <page.json>... --title <title> [container] --attempt fast`
310	        — prints ONE JSON line `{ outcome, key?, reason?, capability?, createPayload? }`.
311	        Run it as ONE plain command (no `cd … &&`, `;`, pipe or redirection):
312	        in a shared repository the tracker-write gate ignores the receipt of
313	        any other shape. A title with a backtick, `$` or `\` goes in a file
314	        passed as `--title-file <path>` in place of `--title <title>`.
315	     4. Act on `outcome` and nothing else: `reused` → return `key`, no
316	        write; `refused` → stop and surface `tracker_idempotency_uncertain`
317	        with `reason`; `create` → the create call below, from the printed
318	        `createPayload`. A `dpt-receipt:` line, printed in a
319	        shared repository, names the receipt the decision wrote.
320	
321	     The prose that follows is the contract those commands implement.
322	
323	     **Never order `summary = <title>`.** Jira ACCEPTS `=` on `summary` and
324	     answers zero rows — a silent always-miss, not a syntax error, so nothing
325	     in the response tells you the probe was broken. Measured read-only
326	     against cloudId `96bffaef-cf5d-4dbf-a170-3d700df9bc83`:
327	     `project = GF AND summary = "The reward banner, repainted light"`
328	     returned `{"issues": [], "isLast": true}`, while
329	     `project = GF AND summary ~ "\"The reward banner, repainted light\""`
330	     returned `GF-83` — exactly one — and `GF-83` provably carries that
331	     summary when fetched by key. An always-missing probe means the retry
332	     path below runs it three times, misses three times, and lands a
333	     duplicate on a board that has no delete tool.
334	
335	     **Order the narrowed query instead.** Conjoin, in this order:
336	
337	     - `project = <projectKey>`;
338	     - the container — `parent = <EpicKey>` for an Epic-keyed milestone,
339	       `labels = "milestone-<M-token>"` for a grandfathered numeric one;
340	     - `issuetype != Epic` — a same-titled Epic is a milestone container,
341	       never an FR to join;
342	     - `labels = "<repo_tag>"` when `### Jira`.repo_tag is declared (a
343	       free-form sub-section field, parsed like `default_labels`);
344	     - `summary ~ "\"<title>\""` — the quoted-phrase form. Without the
345	       escaped inner quotes `~` widens from a phrase match to a word match.
346	
347	     **The query narrows the page; the client decides the join.** `~` is a
348	     text match, never an identity test, so a non-empty page is NOT a hit.
349	     `decide` compares each candidate's summary against `title` under the
350	     ONE normalizer, `normalizeTitleForCompare` (trim, collapse ASCII space
351	     runs, fold en/em dashes and NBSP, drop a heading anchor), and joins
352	     only on that — never re-derive the compare by hand. This is the shape § Milestone Listing already ships twice:
353	     broad JQL then a client-side name filter (Epic leg), broad
354	     `labels IS NOT EMPTY` then a client-side exact-anchored label match
355	     (label leg). The binding path further down already concedes the
356	     principle — "For an Epic-KEYED milestone, summary equality is not the
357	     join" — the create path simply never inherited it.
358	
359	     **A page that reaches the cap is uncertainty, not a miss.** Mirror the
360	     milestone listing's `MILESTONE_PAGE_CAP` treatment: if the last page
361	     still reports `isLast: false`, the ticket has NOT been proven absent. Do not create on it — surface
362	     `tracker_idempotency_uncertain` and let the operator decide.
363	   - **A candidate that fails a conjunct the query carried refuses the
364	     page.** A tracker that honours its own filter never returns another
365	     repository's differently-tagged ticket, an Epic, or a ticket outside the
366	     container, so one on the page means the page came from some other
367	     search. `decide` refuses it as `page-violates-query` with
368	     `tracker_idempotency_uncertain`: re-run the search `query` printed, and
369	     never join or create beside it.
370	   - `mcp__atlassian__createJiraIssue(projectKey=<from CLAUDE.md ### Jira>, summary=title, description=<rendered template>, issuetype=<resolved type>, contentFormat: "markdown")`,
371	     carrying the `createPayload`'s `labels` and, when present, its `parent`
372	     — so the new ticket lands already inside its milestone container and a
373	     retry's narrowed query can find it. Create only on a `create` decision.
374	   - **Network-error retry path (Gateway-Timeout idempotency hardening).**
375	     If the create call returns a network-error response
376	     (Gateway-Timeout / 504 / connection reset / equivalent) instead of a
377	     successful key, the server-side write may have landed despite the
378	     timeout (smoke #6 finding F6: the original write succeeded as `DST-2`
379	     while the timeout caused the retry path to fire). Re-run the JQL
380	     idempotency probe with backoff to give Atlassian's eventual-consistency
381	     window time to settle:
382	
383	     | Attempt | Wait before probe | Action |
384	     |---------|-------------------|--------|
385	     | 1       | 1 second          | The narrowed JQL probe (container conjunct + repo tag + `summary ~` phrase), then the client-side normalized compare |
386	     | 2       | 2 seconds         | Same narrowed JQL probe, same client-side compare |
387	     | 3       | 4 seconds         | Same narrowed JQL probe, same client-side compare |
388	
389	
390	     **Every retry attempt runs the same four steps.** For attempt `N` of
391	     three (`retry-1`, `retry-2`, `retry-3`), after that attempt's wait:
392	
393	     1. `bun run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/adapters/_shared/src/create_idempotency_probe.ts query <projectRoot> --title <title> [container]`;
394	     2. `mcp__atlassian__searchJiraIssuesUsingJql` with the printed `jql` and `fields`;
395	     3. save the page(s), then
396	        `bun run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/adapters/_shared/src/create_idempotency_probe.ts decide <projectRoot> <page.json>... --title <title> [container] --attempt retry-<N>`;
397	     4. act on `outcome`: `reused` → return `key`; `miss` (attempts 1-2
398	        only) → wait and run the next attempt; `refused` → stop with
399	        `tracker_idempotency_uncertain`; `create` (attempt 3 only, no
400	        `repo_tag` declared) → one `mcp__atlassian__createJiraIssue` from
401	        the printed `createPayload`, plus the warning row below.
402	
403	     In a shared repository a create decision authorises one create call:
404	     a create that times out again goes back through `decide`, never
405	     straight to a second create.
406	
407	     Three attempts total; the schedule is `1s + 2s + 4s` (cumulative ~7s
408	     of additional latency on the timeout path only). The single-shot probe
409	     above stays as the fast path — the backoff schedule fires only on the

413	     attempt's compare matches a candidate carrying this repo's tag (or any

423	     - **No `repo_tag` declared** — today's behaviour, unchanged: the

431	       re-run; a spurious create costs a ticket nobody can delete.
432	   - Capture the returned `key` (e.g., `ABC-123`); that's the ticket id.
433	2. Else:
434	   - `mcp__atlassian__editJiraIssue(issueIdOrKey=ticket_id_or_null, fields={ summary, description }, contentFormat: "markdown")`.

449	### `list_project_statuses() → string[]`
450	
451	Fetches the workspace-bound status vocabulary that `/setup` Step Nb
452	uses to seed `specs/tracker-config.yaml`. The fetch is a
453	**two-path probe** dispatched on project style, because the
454	`allowedValues` introspection is company-managed-only (live-MCP behaviour,
455	conformance iter-2 2026-07-02 finding F5):
456	
457	1. **Detect project style** — `mcp__atlassian__getVisibleJiraProjects`
458	   (the same visibility probe `/setup` step 7b already runs; reuse its
459	   response rather than re-calling). A project entry carrying
460	   `"simplified": true` is team-managed (next-gen); absent or `false`
461	   means company-managed.
462	2. **Company-managed ⇒ `allowedValues` path** (the original path,
463	   unchanged). `mcp__atlassian__getJiraIssueTypeMetaWithFields` → the
464	   `status` field's `allowedValues` array; extract each
465	   `allowedValue.name`. This introspection is **company-managed-only**:
466	   team-managed projects return no `allowedValues` for the `status`
467	   field, so an empty result there signals a mis-detected project style,
468	   not an empty workflow.
469	3. **Team-managed ⇒ transitions-derived path** — the **primary** path for
470	   team-managed projects. `mcp__atlassian__getTransitionsForJiraIssue`
471	   against a representative issue in the bound project (or the project's
472	   create-meta default issue type when no issue exists) → collect each
473	   transition's `to.name` in API order, dedup preserving the
474	   first occurrence. (`to.statusCategory` stays available for the
475	   canonical category mapping, same as `transition_status`.)
476	
477	Both paths return the same output contract: an ordered string array
478	of status names, verbatim casing and whitespace — so the
479	`tracker-config.yaml` composition is untouched by the dispatch.
480	
481	**Zero-issue edge.** A fresh team-managed project with no issues offers
482	nothing to call `getTransitionsForJiraIssue` against: fall back to the
483	three canonical `statusCategory` names (`To Do` / `In Progress` / `Done`)
484	and surface a `tracker_config_write_mcp_unavailable`-style advisory so the
485	operator knows the seeded vocabulary is a category-level approximation of
486	the workflow, not its real named states.
487	
488	Project key is sourced from `### Jira`.project in CLAUDE.md via
489	`readWorkspaceBinding(claudeMdPath, "jira")`; the issue type defaults to
490	`Task` (or the `jira_issue_type:` override). Reject with NFR-10 canonical
491	shape when the project key is unresolved (mirrors the create-path
492	silent-landing guard). Pure read; no mutation.

494	## Project Milestone — milestone-as-Epic via `parent`, label fallback
495	
496	Jira opts into project-milestone binding (`project_milestone: true` in the
497	frontmatter). Jira has no per-issue "milestone" field on the standard MCP
498	surface, but it does have a native container: the **Epic**. The primary
499	binding (`milestone_binding: epic` in the frontmatter) realises each
500	milestone as an Epic issue created under its human title, from whose
501	tracker-assigned key the milestone id is derived; the
502	FR Task binds by pointing its `parent` field at that Epic's key. When the
503	bound project has no Epic type (or cannot set `parent`), the binding
504	degrades to the legacy **label** path documented further down — never a
505	hard failure.
506	
507	### Epic path (primary — `milestone_binding: epic`)
508	
509	**Find.** Enumerate the project's Epics via
510	`mcp__atlassian__searchJiraIssuesUsingJql` with
511	`jql = "project = <projectKey> AND issuetype = Epic"` and match the milestone's
512	Epic by KEY when the plan heading carries an `M_<key>` token: sanitize each
513	candidate's key forward (`GF-78` → `M_GF_78`) and compare. For an Epic-KEYED
514	milestone, summary equality is not the join — the canonical name embeds the
515	very key being looked for, while the Epic itself carries the human title typed
516	at creation. A name that carries NO token — a pre-key human title, the state
517	between minting the Epic and writing the plan file — has no key to compare, so
518	that one arm still matches by NAME, byte-exactly. Both arms refuse on a miss:
519	binding never creates.
520	
521	**Mint — create, read the key back, derive the id, then write the plan file.**
522	A milestone Epic is minted in the only order whose values exist at the moment
523	each is needed. `adapters/_shared/src/mint_milestone_epic.ts` performs steps
524	1–3; its caller performs step 4. Step 1 is wrapped in a find-before-create
525	retry on the canonical `1s + 2s + 4s` schedule: a create that lands in Jira and
526	then times out is FOUND on the retry and reused, never created a second time.
527	That protection is why a timeout does not mint a duplicate Epic.
528	
529	1. Create the Epic with the **human title alone** —
530	   `mcp__atlassian__createJiraIssue(projectKey=<projectKey>,
531	   issueTypeName="Epic", summary=<human title>)`. The canonical
532	   `M_<key> — <Title>` name is not available here: it embeds the key Jira is
533	   about to allocate for this very Epic, so ordering it would order a value
534	   that does not yet exist.
535	2. **read the key back** from the create response, verbatim (`GF-78`).
536	3. **derive the id** from that key via `milestoneIdFromEpicKey` (`GF-78` →
537	   `M_GF_78`); a key that will not sanitize into a well-formed id refuses
538	   rather than yielding a malformed one.
539	4. **write the plan file** under that id, with heading `## M_<key> — <Title>`.
540	
541	**Epic label — at mint time only.** After it derives the id, and outside the
542	step-1 retry, the mint writes the label `milestone-M_<key>` on the Epic itself
543	(`milestone-M_GF_78` for `GF-78`). That label is a read-side convenience: it
544	lets a repo enumerating a shared project find the milestone by its label. It
545	is never the binding surface — membership stays the FR's `parent`, below. A
546	failed label write never fails the mint: the Epic and its derived id stand,
547	and only the convenience is missing. In a live session the write is a
548	read-merge-write on the Epic's own key —
549	`mcp__atlassian__editJiraIssue(issueIdOrKey=<epic-key>,
550	additional_fields={ labels: [...<existing labels>, "milestone-M_<key>"] })`,
551	never clobbering a label already there. `mintMilestoneEpic` performs it
552	through the provider's `addLabel` and reports whether it landed as
553	`labelled`; its command form prints the label it would write as
554	`label=milestone-M_<key>` beside the derived id.
555	
556	**Joining, never minting.** A repo joining a container another repo already
557	minted calls the mint with `{ join: true }`. Its find leg compares titles
558	after normalizing whitespace and case: exactly one match joins that Epic, two
559	or more refuse and name every candidate with its key, and no match — or a
560	provider carrying no `listEpics` — refuses instead of creating. A join never
561	creates. The toolkit makes every other mint with the approved decision of
562	`resolve_milestone_identity.ts` as `expect`, so it performs that act or refuses; only a bare mint with neither option still finds by title.
563	
564	The mint surfaces NO capability row: it is a step of its own, not an attach
565	outcome, and the attach that follows FINDS the Epic and returns `capability:
566	null`. `milestone_create_required` belongs to the object binding's
567	`save_milestone` auto-create, which this path never reaches.
568	
569	**Membership — `parent` set.** Bind the FR Task by writing the Epic's key to
570	its `parent` field: `mcp__atlassian__editJiraIssue(issueIdOrKey=ticket_id,
571	additional_fields={ parent: { key: <epic-key> } })`. This path never touches
572	milestone objects. For an Epic-KEYED milestone the per-FR attach writes no
573	`milestone-<M-token>` label on the FR ticket; the only `milestone-M_<key>`
574	label such a milestone carries is the one the mint writes on the Epic itself.
575	A grandfathered NUMERIC `M<N>` milestone under this same binding deliberately
576	DOES take the label surface on the ticket, because that is where the reader's
577	own grandfather clause looks for it; see the numeric note below.
578	Idempotency pre-check: the issue is read FIRST, before any Epic is listed
579	(STE-611). When its binding is already present the attach is a no-op, with
580	no enumeration and no write, even when that parent Epic lives in another
581	project (a legacy `GB-40` parent under a repository now bound to `GF`).
582	
583	**Read-back verify.** Re-read the issue (`getJiraIssue`) and assert
584	`parent = <epic-key>`. A mismatch surfaces the canonical binding-mismatch
585	error (never retried); transient failures retry the whole round-trip on the
586	canonical `1s + 2s + 4s` schedule.
587	
588	**Grandfathered numeric milestones — the numeric note.** A project that adopts
589	Epic-keyed milestones still has its old numeric `M<N>` ones. Under this same
590	`milestone_binding: epic`, a numeric token does NOT bind by parent Epic: it
591	takes the `milestone-M<N>` LABEL surface, through the same read-merge-write
592	attach the legacy binding uses. That is not an inconsistency — it is the only
593	arrangement that converges, because the reader's own grandfather clause looks
594	for a numeric milestone on the label surface. Binding by parent while the
595	reader checks labels is what made a backfill sweep report the same work done on
596	every pass forever. There is nothing to configure: the routing is decided by
597	the milestone TOKEN's kind, not by the adapter's declared binding.
598	
599	**Epic-absent fallback.** Probe the bound project's issue-type metadata via
600	`mcp__atlassian__getJiraProjectIssueTypesMetadata`. When the Epic type is
601	absent — or the project cannot set `parent` — the attach degrades to the
602	label path below and the closing summary surfaces the **informational**
603	`milestone_epic_unsupported` capability row (the FR still attaches via the
604	legacy label; the degraded path is never an error).
605	
606	### Label path (fallback — legacy `milestone_binding: label`)
607	
608	Each FR's frontmatter `milestone: M<N>` maps to the
609	`milestone-<M-token>` label (e.g. `milestone-M86`), and the milestone-attach
610	flow (`/spec-write` § 0b, `/implement` Phase 1 step 0.e) attaches that label
611	to the pushed ticket.
612	
613	**Mapping.** FR `milestone: M<N>` → the `milestone-<M-token>` label. The
614	token is the raw milestone token (`M86`), giving labels like
615	`milestone-M86`. The label is created implicitly the first time it is
616	attached — there is no pre-existing tracker milestone object to look up
617	(this is the `N/A (create-on-write)` missing-milestone handling from
618	`docs/tracker-adapters.md`).
619	
620	**Attach — `editJiraIssue` read-merge-write.** Jira's MCP has no top-level
621	`labels` parameter on the edit path and no append-a-label operation; a
622	naive write would clobber every other label on the issue. So the attach is
623	a **read-merge-write** cycle:
624	
625	1. **Read** — `mcp__atlassian__getJiraIssue(issueIdOrKey=ticket_id)` and
626	   capture the issue's current `labels` array.
627	2. **Merge** — union the existing labels with `milestone-<M-token>`; if the
628	   label is already present this is a no-op set (idempotent).
629	3. **Write** — `mcp__atlassian__editJiraIssue(issueIdOrKey=ticket_id,
630	   additional_fields={ labels: <merged set> })` with the full merged array,
631	   so no pre-existing label is dropped. (There is no top-level `labels`
632	   parameter — labels go through `additional_fields.labels`, the same path
633	   the on-create `default_labels` rule uses; see the MCP tool-names table.)
634	
635	**Read-back verify.** After the write, **re-read** the issue
636	(`getJiraIssue`) and assert the `milestone-<M-token>` label is present in
637	the returned `labels` — the read-back verify confirms the attach landed
638	(the same silent-no-op discipline the metadata writes use). If the label is
639	absent on read-back, surface an NFR-10 canonical-shape warning rather than
640	reporting success.
641	
642	**`default_labels` carve-out (on-create only).** The `### Jira`.default_labels
643	workspace-binding field applies **only on create** (`createJiraIssue`),
644	per the workspace-binding rule documented under `upsert_ticket_metadata`.
645	The milestone-attach read-merge-write runs on the **edit** path and is
646	entirely independent of `default_labels`: it neither reads nor reapplies
647	`default_labels`, and attaching a milestone label never re-triggers the
648	create-time default-labels behaviour. Conversely, a create that seeds
649	`default_labels` does not attach the milestone label — milestone binding is
650	always its own explicit read-merge-write step.
651	
652	## Milestone Listing — `listMilestones()` via Epic enumeration + grandfathered labels
653	
654	The Jira `AdapterDriver` implements the optional `listMilestones()` method so
655	the tracker leg of `nextFreeMilestoneNumber` fires in Jira mode. With the
656	Epic-first binding (§ Project Milestone above), *listing* milestones means
657	*enumerating milestone Epics* — a handful of objects, never a full
658	labelled-task scan — with the legacy `milestone-<M-token>` labels unioned in
659	as a grandfathered second leg so pre-Epic milestones stay visible. That leg
660	is no longer legacy-only: it is also the only route that sees a freshly
661	minted Epic, which carries the `milestone-M_<key>` label the mint writes but
662	not yet a summary that leads with a milestone token.
663	
664	**Pure-function core.** The two-leg scan + pagination + dedupe logic lives in
665	the Schema-P helper `adapters/jira/src/list_milestones.ts`
666	(`listMilestones(fetchPage, opts?)`; the Epic leg injects via
667	`opts.fetchEpicPage`), mirroring `discover_field.ts`: no network in the
668	function itself — the caller injects the fetchers, which wrap the MCP calls.
669	`TrackerProvider.listMilestones()` already delegates
670	`driver.listMilestones?.() ?? []`, so no provider change is needed; the Jira
671	driver simply supplies this method.
672	
673	**Procedure (driver wiring).**
674	
675	1. **Epic leg (primary)** — `mcp__atlassian__searchJiraIssuesUsingJql` with
676	   `jql = "project = <projectKey> AND issuetype = Epic ORDER BY created DESC"`
677	   (project key from `### Jira`.project), paginating page by page. Feed each
678	   raw search answer, verbatim — plain or wrapped — into the helper's `fetchEpicPage`.
679	   Client-side name filter: an Epic counts iff its summary's first
680	   whitespace-delimited word is a valid milestone token (union grammar); each
681	   match contributes `M_<epic-key>` (key verbatim).
682	2. **Label leg (grandfathered labels and freshly minted Epics)** — the same JQL tool with
683	   `jql = "project = <projectKey> AND labels IS NOT EMPTY ORDER BY created DESC"`,
684	   feeding each raw search answer, verbatim, into `fetchPage`.
685	   This JQL deliberately carries no `issuetype` filter, and that absence is
686	   what lets the label leg return an Epic carrying the `milestone-M_<epic-key>`
687	   label the mint writes — so a repo joining a shared project finds a freshly
688	   minted Epic even before its summary is renamed to lead with a milestone
689	   token (the only thing the Epic leg in step 1 counts); adding an `issuetype`
690	   filter to this JQL would hide those Epics.
691	   Client-side, each label is matched against the exact-anchored union shape
692	   `^milestone-(<M-token>)$` — accepting `milestone-M<N>` and
693	   `milestone-M_<epic-key>` while `milestone-foo`, `milestone-`,
694	   `xmilestone-M5`, `M5`, `milestone-M5-extra`, `milestone-M5 ` all stay
695	   rejected, matching the create-on-write `milestone-<M-token>` derivation.
696	3. **Return** — the deduped union of both legs as bare tokens
697	   (`{ name }[]` of `M<N>` / `M_<epic-key>` — **not** the `milestone-`
698	   label), numeric tokens first ascending, epic-keyed tokens after (opaque,
699	   code-point order) — so the existing `scanTracker` extractor in
700	   `next_free_milestone_number.ts` consumes it unchanged and `M_<key>` ids
701	   never bump the sequential counter.
702	
703	**Pagination cap, no silent truncation.** Each leg paginates to a documented
704	cap (`MILESTONE_PAGE_CAP`, default 50; overridable via `opts.pageCap`). If the
705	cap is reached before a page proves it is the last (plain `isLast`, or wrapped
706	`issues.pageInfo.hasNextPage: false`), the helper stops that leg and
707	surfaces a one-line log (`opts.log`) noting pages may have been dropped —
708	never a silent truncation.
709	
710	**Fail-soft / non-load-bearing.** Any JQL / network failure — including a
711	failure on a later page of either leg — degrades `listMilestones()` to `[]`;
712	it never throws into allocation. Identical posture to Linear's milestone leg
713	and the cross-branch git leg.
714	
715	> **Supersedes.** The Epic leg supersedes the label-only listing that closed
716	> the deferred *listing* half of the create-on-write `milestone-<M-token>`
717	> label binding (itself superseding the never-shipped "Jira milestone API"
718	> enumeration). Grandfathered labels remain listed via the union so pre-Epic
719	> milestones never disappear; attach (write) and listing (read) stay
720	> orthogonal halves of the same milestone model. (Ticket-level traceability
721	> lives in the FR + git history, not in this shipped adapter doc.)

The toolkit under test is <toolkit>/plugins/dev-process-toolkit. Run every toolkit script from exactly that path, as bun "<toolkit>/plugins/dev-process-toolkit/adapters/_shared/src/<name>.ts", and never from a plugin cache, an installed copy, or a path you resolve yourself: $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is empty inside a Bash call, so a bare script name is yours to resolve, and resolving it elsewhere grades a version nobody is testing.
FOUR RULES FOR EVERY STEP OF THIS SESSION. Each carries its reason, because each was broken by a child doing something ordinary and sensible, and a rule without its reason reads as style and gets optimised away.
1. **ONE OPERATION PER BASH CALL.** No `;`, no `&&`, no trailing `echo "exit=$?"`, no second command of any kind beside the one being graded. Two separate mechanisms punish chaining and a child told only one of them will keep breaking the other. For a **toolkit module**: the recorded `exitCode` belongs to the command's LAST segment, so `bun <module>; echo "exit=$?"` records the echo's zero, and seven predicates gate on the module's exact exit code — the echo you added to preserve the status is what destroys it. For **git**: one command yields one subcommand, so `git merge …; git ci …` is read as a merge and the second invocation is invisible. Name the module by its FULL ABSOLUTE PATH in the same command that runs it: `S=…; bun "$S/adapters/_shared/src/x.ts"` is unreadable for a second and independent reason — the target is not absolute at the point it is parsed — so splitting the chain without also inlining the path fixes nothing. Measured on leg 4: whole scenarios whose work was done correctly and never seen. The verdict's `observations` carry the live count for a given run; no number is written here, because the instrument that counts them is itself under repair and a document pinning its output is stale by construction.
2. **FETCH EVERY LISTING; NEVER FABRICATE ONE.** Any file a command reads as a tracker listing must come from a real MCP call. **FABRICATING is forbidden** — typing rows, inventing objects, editing values, or repairing an answer you did not like. **PROJECTING a fetched answer into the shape a documented flag requires is NOT fabricating, and is sometimes the documented procedure** — the distinction is whether every value in the file came out of the tracker. **Omitting or adding fields is neither fabricating nor projecting: save the answer whole.** A file with fields deleted, trimmed, added or filled in passes that test and is still not the tracker's answer. Leg 8 measured all four: children dropped `context` (which broke S14's shape detection), trimmed URLs and avatars, had `jq` add a `requestCursor`, and had `sed` invent a `creator` by copying `reporter` — manufactured tracker data, then fed to an ownership decision. This rule previously read "do not reshape it", which forbade the projection too, and that wording aborted live leg 5 at step 2: the child fetched Jira statuses the documented way for a team-managed project (`getTransitionsForJiraIssue`, which answers `{transitions:[{to:{name}}]}`), found the flag wanted a `statuses` array, and correctly refused rather than break the rule. It had no legal path, which is the failure mode this programme has now produced twice. That specific case no longer needs a projection at all — `repoint_tracker_binding.ts` accepts both documented shapes and projects `to.name` itself, so the transformation lives in one tested place rather than in twenty-six prompts — but the distinction stands for any flag that still needs one. The modules validate the answer's shape and refuse anything else, and a hand-built input into a file a gate reads is indistinguishable from fabricated evidence. The ONE exception is Jira `--labels`, which no Atlassian tool lists; everything else, statuses included, is fetchable — see `docs/setup-reference.md` § Repoint preconditions. Leg 4's step 9 called `searchJiraIssuesUsingJql`, had the real answer in hand, and typed a file anyway; the module refused it and the scenario died there.
3. **RUN A MODULE DIRECTLY; NEVER THROUGH A WRAPPER.** Invoke `bun "<the module path>"` as its own command. Do not write a script that imports the module and prints your own summary. A wrapper can filter, reformat, swallow a throw, or print a count the module never produced, so the grader does not accept one and is right not to — a script that imports X is not a run of X. Two different children wrote wrappers on leg 4, so this is a habit rather than one child's improvisation; a child that meets the refusal should fix the invocation rather than conclude the harness is broken.
4. **A REFUSAL IS INFORMATION; READ WHAT IT NAMES.** Every toolkit refusal names the offending shape and a remedy. Fix what it names and retry. Do not conclude a step is impossible because one command was refused — and when the refusal blocked a chained call, note that everything after it never ran either.

A path without the run's nonce survives from run to run: on leg 8, /tmp/dpt-s8/ still held 2026-09-23 listings, one naming a key that no longer existed, beside that day's.

1	# `/spec-write` Tracker Mode Flow
2	
3	> See `docs/layout-reference.md` — canonical authority on FR file shape (per-FR file path, AC-prefix derivation, `## Acceptance Criteria` section).
4	
5	Detailed tracker-mode procedures for `/spec-write`. Pointed at from
6	`skills/spec-write/SKILL.md` step 0 to keep the skill under NFR-1.
7	
8	In `mode: none`, this document is unused.
9	
10	## Tracker ID Assignment Order
11	
12	**Rule:** create the tracker ticket **first**, read the returned ID, substitute the placeholder globally, **then** write the FR file. **Never guess** the next sequential tracker number.
13	
14	The order is load-bearing. Trackers skip cancelled numbers, renumber across workspace renames, and allocate IDs atomically on ticket creation — an implementer's guess ("`<TKR>-NN` was last, so the next is `<TKR>-NN+1`") can be wrong silently, and the misalignment ships into every downstream artifact (AC prefixes, filename, plan-file row, every prose cross-reference).
15	
16	### Concrete flow
17	
18	1. **Draft with placeholder.** Use `<tracker-id>` (or adapter-specific rendering — `STE-<N>` for Linear, `PROJ-<N>` for Jira) throughout the draft:
19	   - AC lines: `AC-<tracker-id>.1`, `AC-<tracker-id>.2`, …
20	   - Filename: `<tracker-id>.md`
21	   - Plan-file table row: `| <tracker-id> | Title | <tracker>:<tracker-id> |`
22	   - Prose cross-references: `"closes <tracker-id>"`, `"supersedes <tracker-id>"`
23	2. **Create the tracker ticket.** Call `Provider.sync(spec)` → `upsertTicketMetadata(null, …)`. **Workspace binding.** Before invoking, call `readWorkspaceBinding(claudeMdPath, "linear" | "jira")` from `adapters/_shared/src/workspace_binding.ts` and pass `team` + `project` + `defaultLabels` into the call so the new ticket lands on the correct project board with the configured labels. Linear adapter rejects creates that lack `project` per the silent-landing trap; Jira adapter rejects creates that lack `project` per the Jira API requirement. **Labels** are optional and forwarded only when `defaultLabels` is populated (Linear → `save_issue.labels`; Jira → `createJiraIssue.additional_fields.labels`). The tracker allocator returns the real ID (e.g., `<TKR>-NN`).
24	3. **Substitute globally.** Replace every `<tracker-id>` with the returned ID in one pass.
25	4. **Write the FR file.** Only after substitution completes — the file on disk never contains a placeholder.
26	
27	### Worked example
28	
29	Draft AC line: `AC-<tracker-id>.1: releaseLock asserts pre-state in_progress`
30	
31	Linear assigns the next free ID (let's call it `<TKR>-NN`) on save.
32	
33	Final AC line in file: `AC-<TKR>-NN.1: releaseLock asserts pre-state in_progress`
34	Filename: `specs/frs/<TKR>-NN.md`
35	Plan row: `| <TKR>-NN | Hide full 26-char ULIDs | linear:<TKR>-NN |`
36	
37	### Mode: none exemption
38	
39	Mode: none projects mint the short-ULID tail locally (collision-proof by Crockford Base32 randomness + scan). No tracker allocator, no race. The placeholder rule is tracker-mode only.
40	
41	## Post-save behavior (tracker mode)
42	
43	After each AC-list save in `specs/frs/<tracker-id>.md`'s
44	`## Acceptance Criteria` section:
45	
46	1. Resolve the ticket-id for the edited FR directly from the filename
47	   (`<tracker-id>.md`) — the filename IS the binding, no separate
48	   traceability matrix is consulted. If the FR is brand-new and the
49	   filename still carries the `<tracker-id>` placeholder, prompt the
50	   user for a fresh `upsert_ticket_metadata(null, ...)` invocation that
51	   creates the ticket and substitutes the returned ID per the
52	   placeholder rule above.
53	2. Run ticket-binding confirmation per `docs/ticket-binding.md`.
54	3. Call `pull_acs(ticket_id)` — fresh fetch, just like `/implement` does.
55	4. Classify the local AC list vs the tracker AC list via the bidirectional
56	   diff classifier (`adapters/_shared/src/classify_diff.ts`). Full procedure
57	   in `docs/ac-sync.md`.
58	5. If any AC is non-`identical`, surface the Schema K diff and run the
59	   per-AC prompt loop. **Cancel aborts the save** — local changes revert
60	   to the in-memory draft state (the user re-decides).
61	6. On resolution (including `all identical` fast path), call
62	   `upsert_ticket_metadata(ticket_id, title, <rebuilt description>)` to
63	   push the converged state to the tracker.
64	   `git log` captures the sync event via the commit; no separate audit
65	   trail is written.
66	
67	`/spec-write` on a brand-new FR (no ticket bound yet) skips steps 1–5 and
68	goes straight to `upsert_ticket_metadata(null, title, description)` to
69	mint a new ticket; the returned ID becomes the FR filename
70	(`specs/frs/<tracker-id>.md`) — the filename IS the binding (no
71	separate traceability matrix is maintained).
72	
73	## Cancel semantics
74	
75	- **During diff/resolve cancel (step 5):** local draft stays in memory;
76	  tracker untouched. User can retry or abandon.
77	- **During mint-new cancel:** no `upsert_ticket_metadata` call; no FR
78	  file is written to disk (the draft stays in memory — cancel here means
79	  "don't push to tracker, don't land the file yet").
80	
81	## Orphan listing
82	
83	`/spec-write` § 0.5 never improvises the tracker-orphan list. Fetch the
84	container with the adapter's `list_active_frs` read (see `adapters/jira.md`
85	and `adapters/linear.md`), save every page verbatim as a JSON file, then run:
86	
87	```bash
88	bun run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/adapters/_shared/src/container_ownership.ts list <projectRoot> <page.json>...
89	```
90	
91	Page fields the listing needs:
92	
93	- **Jira** (`searchJiraIssuesUsingJql`, paginated to `isLast: true`): `key`,
94	  `summary`, `issuetype`, `labels`, `description`, `creator`, `project`.
95	- **Linear** (`list_issues`, cursor followed to `hasNextPage: false`):
96	  `id` / `identifier`, `title`, `labels`, `description`, `createdBy`,
97	  `project`, `team`.
98	
99	A repository that declares a shared tracker refuses a page whose ticket lacks
100	`labels` or `description`, naming the file or the key; a missing or non-JSON
101	page file refuses too, and nothing is listed from a page that failed to parse.
102	
103	The listing prints one table row per unbound ticket — `Key`, `Class`, `Owner`
104	(the creator), `Toolkit-written` (the `Source: specs/frs/<key>.md` back-link,
105	reported only; it is not ownership evidence) and `Title` — then a `summary:`
106	line counting every class, the excluded ones included. Classes: `ours` (carries
107	this repository's `repo_tag`), `unowned` (no owner label — hand-filed, or a
108	client too old to tag), `sibling` (another repository's label) and `container`
109	(a Jira Epic or any hierarchy level above the FR). `sibling` and `container`
110	tickets are counted and never offered. Each offerable ticket gets one line
111	carrying the two option labels to show verbatim:
112	
113	```
114	options: Import <KEY> | Skip <KEY>
115	```
116	
117	On an explicit `Import <KEY>` answer, record consent before the import:
118	
119	```bash
120	bun run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/adapters/_shared/src/container_ownership.ts consent <projectRoot> <KEY> <page.json>...
121	```
122	
123	`consent` re-classifies the same pages and, in a shared repository, writes an
124	`import` receipt for an `ours` or `unowned` key only; it refuses a `sibling`,
125	`container` or unlisted key with nothing written. An undeclared repository
126	writes no receipt.
127	
128	Then hand the same saved pages to the import as its ownership context,
129	`importFromTracker(trackerKey, trackerId, provider, specsDir, promptMilestone,
130	{ projectRoot, pages })`. With the pages, a `sibling` or `container` key
131	refuses before any write. Importing an `unowned` ticket claims it: the sync
132	adds this repository's tag to the labels the page shows, so the sibling's next
133	listing classifies it `sibling`. In a shared repository, a page that lacks the
134	ticket or its `labels` refuses rather than risk a label set that drops a
135	label. Where the tag write never lands, probe #49's `bound-ticket-untagged`
136	row names the ticket.
137	
138	## MCP call budget (NFR-8)
139	
140	Per FR save: at most **1** MCP call (`upsert_ticket_metadata`, ≤ 1 per
141	spec). The additional `pull_acs` in step 3 is shared with the same skill's
142	pre-flight work and counts toward the 2-call `/implement` budget in
143	sessions where `/spec-write` chains into `/implement`.

32	# Jira Adapter
33	
34	> Verified against live MCP 2026-04-29 (smoke-test #5).
35	
36	ACs live in one of two places, dispatched by the value of the existing
37	top-level Schema L key `jira_ac_field:` under `## Task Tracking`:
38	
39	- `jira_ac_field: customfield_XXXXX` — per-tenant **custom field** path. The
40	  GID varies per Jira project; `/setup` runs `/rest/api/3/field`
41	  introspection (via `discover_field.ts`) and records the GID. AC reads /
42	  writes go through that field.
43	- `jira_ac_field: description` — **description-body** path (sentinel value).
44	  No custom field exists in this project (or the operator opted out of
45	  creating one — common for team-managed Kanban templates that ship without
46	  one). AC reads / writes parse and rewrite the bullet list under the
47	  `## Acceptance Criteria` heading inside the issue's description body. The
48	  heading is the parse anchor; bullets outside that section are ignored on
49	  read; `push_ac_toggle` rewrites the entire `## Acceptance Criteria` section
50	  atomically.
51	
52	`jira_ac_field:` is the same canonical Schema L key in both cases — no new
53	key was added. The discriminator is the value: any string matching
54	`customfield_\d+` is a custom-field GID; the literal string `description`
55	is the description-body sentinel; any other value is rejected with
56	NFR-10 canonical shape during `/setup`.
57	
58	## MCP tool names
59	
60	| Operation | MCP tool | Notes |
61	|-----------|----------|-------|
62	| `pull_acs` | `mcp__atlassian__getJiraIssue` | Branches on `jira_ac_field`: read the custom-field value (custom-field path) or the issue's description body (description path) and parse `## Acceptance Criteria` bullets. |
63	| `push_ac_toggle` | `mcp__atlassian__editJiraIssue` | Branches on `jira_ac_field`: write back the toggled custom-field value or rewrite the description's `## Acceptance Criteria` section atomically. Pass `contentFormat: "markdown"` to round-trip markdown without ADF conversion. |
64	| `transition_status` | `mcp__atlassian__transitionJiraIssue` | Resolve transition id via `getTransitionsForJiraIssue` + `status_mapping`. Primary match is `to.name`; fallback is `to.statusCategory.key` (canonical category). |
65	| `upsert_ticket_metadata` | `mcp__atlassian__createJiraIssue` (new) / `mcp__atlassian__editJiraIssue` (existing) | Body MUST include the back-link to `specs/frs/<TICKET-ID>.md`. On create, `project` is required (Jira API requirement) — sourced from the call argument or `### Jira`.project in CLAUDE.md; reject with NFR-10 canonical shape if neither supplies a value. `team` does not apply to Jira and is silently dropped if forwarded. **Labels:** when `### Jira`.default_labels is populated (free-form sub-section field, parsed as inline-YAML array per `docs/patterns.md`) **or** the call argument carries `labels`, forward every entry into `createJiraIssue.additional_fields.labels` (the only Jira-MCP path for setting labels — there is no top-level `labels` parameter, see the `mcp__atlassian__createJiraIssue` schema). Empty array or missing key ⇒ no `labels` field is set. **Update path** (`editJiraIssue`): labels are not modified — `defaultLabels` applies only on create per the workspace-binding rule. The one exception is the claim on import in a shared repository: importing an `unowned` ticket sends `labels` as the union of the ticket's current labels (read off the saved container page) and this repository's ownership tag, never a set that drops a label (`docs/spec-write-tracker-mode.md` § Orphan listing). 77	### Silent no-op trap
78	
79	Any write operation that addresses fields or transitions Jira doesn't know
80	about (unknown field GIDs, transition IDs that don't exist in the current
81	workflow) can return a successful-looking response while mutating nothing
82	on the ticket. There is no canonical validation error for "unknown field"
83	in every Jira MCP; the caller can't distinguish success from silent no-op
84	by the response shape alone.
85	
86	**Rule for every write caller:** after the call, re-fetch the ticket and
87	assert that at least one of `updated` / `statuscategorychangedate` (or the
88	Jira-MCP equivalent of Linear's `updatedAt` / `startedAt` / `completedAt`)
89	advanced past the pre-call value before treating the call as successful.
90	If none advanced, the write was silently no-op'd — treat it as a hard
91	failure and surface an NFR-10 canonical-shape error.
92	
93	`adapters/_shared/src/tracker_provider.ts` encodes this as
94	`TrackerWriteNoOpError`; `TrackerProvider.claimLock` and
95	`TrackerProvider.releaseLock` perform the post-call `updatedAt` check
96	automatically for every adapter, not just Linear. Adapter driver
97	implementations MUST populate `TicketStatusSummary.updatedAt` so the guard
98	can fire — see `docs/tracker-adapters.md` § Silent no-op trap for the
99	cross-adapter pattern and `adapters/linear.md` § Silent no-op trap for the
100	reference implementation that was dogfooded against a live MCP.
101	
102	### claimLock-skipped trap
103	
104	Symmetric trap on the release side. If `/implement` Phase 1 step 0.c
105	(`Provider.claimLock`) is skipped — either by a manual invocation that
106	started later than entry, or by a session that resumed mid-run without
107	the claim firing — the Jira ticket stays in `Backlog` (or equivalent
108	pre-start status) while implementation proceeds. At Phase 4 Close, a
109	naive `releaseLock` would call `transitionStatus('done')` and leap
110	`Backlog → Done`, skipping `In Progress` entirely (no `startedAt`-like
111	timestamp ever set on the Jira ticket).
112	
113	`TrackerProvider.releaseLock` now re-fetches the ticket's current status
114	before `transitionStatus` and asserts the pre-state is `"in_progress"`.
115	Any other pre-state (`backlog`, `unstarted`, `cancelled`, `done`,
116	`completed`) raises `TrackerReleaseLockPreconditionError` without calling
117	`transitionStatus`. Complement to the post-write `TrackerWriteNoOpError`:
118	pre-write asserts the ticket is in the expected state, post-write asserts
119	the write landed. Both layers together make `releaseLock` fail-closed.
120	
121	No extra MCP call — the pre-state check reuses the `getTicketStatus`
122	fetch that the post-write `updatedAt` guard already does (NFR-8 call
123	budget preserved). The error carries the ticket ref, tracker key, and
124	observed status; operators fix either by transitioning the ticket to
125	`In Progress` manually or by rerunning `/implement` from Phase 1 so
126	`claimLock` fires. This guard is adapter-agnostic — the shared code fires
127	regardless of whether the driver is `linear`, `jira`, or a custom adapter.

135	## Space pre-creation (manual prerequisite)
136	
137	The Atlassian Rovo MCP exposes no project-creation tool, so the operator
138	**must create the Space (Jira project) in the Jira UI before running
139	`/setup`**. `/setup` for `mode: jira` records the project key in the
140	`### Jira` sub-section under `## Task Tracking`; on every subsequent run,
141	the adapter validates that the configured key is visible to the
142	authenticated principal via `mcp__atlassian__getVisibleJiraProjects`.
143	
144	If the project is **not visible** (key typo, OAuth principal lacks
145	membership, project archived), refuse with NFR-10 canonical shape:
146	
147	```
148	Jira project '<key>' not visible to the authenticated principal.
149	Remedy: create the Space in the Jira UI before running /setup, or grant the OAuth principal membership; then re-run the failing skill — `/setup` for first-time recording, `/setup --migrate` to re-record an already-bound project key.
150	Context: mode=jira, project=<key>, skill=<caller>
151	```
152	
153	Refusing here is load-bearing: a silent fall-through would let Jira
154	operations fail later with opaque permission errors. Visibility check is
155	~50ms and runs before any other Jira call (NFR-8 call budget).

293	     create call fires, look for a ticket this FR already minted on a prior
294	     run (resume / retry) and return that id without writing.
295	
296	     **The decision is a command, not prose.** Run these four steps in order,
297	     with the milestone container flag (`--parent <EpicKey>` for an
298	     Epic-keyed milestone, `--milestone-label <label>` for a grandfathered
299	     numeric one) passed identically to both commands:
300	
301	     1. `bun run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/adapters/_shared/src/create_idempotency_probe.ts query <projectRoot> --title <title> [container]`
302	        — prints ONE JSON line `{ "jql": …, "fields": [...] }`. It reads
303	        `### Jira`.`repo_tag` (a free-form sub-section field, parsed like
304	        `default_labels`) from the binding itself (no tag is ever passed
305	        by hand) and refuses, non-zero, a tag the create would not forward.
306	     2. `mcp__atlassian__searchJiraIssuesUsingJql` with exactly that `jql`
307	        and those `fields` — no edits to either.
308	     3. Save every returned page verbatim as a JSON file (each page after the first with its `requestCursor`, the cursor it was fetched with), then
309	        `bun run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/adapters/_shared/src/create_idempotency_probe.ts decide <projectRoot> <page.json>... --title <title> [container] --attempt fast`
310	        — prints ONE JSON line `{ outcome, key?, reason?, capability?, createPayload? }`.
311	        Run it as ONE plain command (no `cd … &&`, `;`, pipe or redirection):
312	        in a shared repository the tracker-write gate ignores the receipt of
313	        any other shape. A title with a backtick, `$` or `\` goes in a file
314	        passed as `--title-file <path>` in place of `--title <title>`.
315	     4. Act on `outcome` and nothing else: `reused` → return `key`, no
316	        write; `refused` → stop and surface `tracker_idempotency_uncertain`
317	        with `reason`; `create` → the create call below, from the printed
318	        `createPayload`. A `dpt-receipt:` line, printed in a
319	        shared repository, names the receipt the decision wrote.
320	
321	     The prose that follows is the contract those commands implement.
322	
323	     **Never order `summary = <title>`.** Jira ACCEPTS `=` on `summary` and
324	     answers zero rows — a silent always-miss, not a syntax error, so nothing
325	     in the response tells you the probe was broken. Measured read-only
326	     against cloudId `96bffaef-cf5d-4dbf-a170-3d700df9bc83`:
327	     `project = GF AND summary = "The reward banner, repainted light"`
328	     returned `{"issues": [], "isLast": true}`, while
329	     `project = GF AND summary ~ "\"The reward banner, repainted light\""`
330	     returned `GF-83` — exactly one — and `GF-83` provably carries that
331	     summary when fetched by key. An always-missing probe means the retry
332	     path below runs it three times, misses three times, and lands a
333	     duplicate on a board that has no delete tool.
334	
335	     **Order the narrowed query instead.** Conjoin, in this order:
336	
337	     - `project = <projectKey>`;
338	     - the container — `parent = <EpicKey>` for an Epic-keyed milestone,
339	       `labels = "milestone-<M-token>"` for a grandfathered numeric one;
340	     - `issuetype != Epic` — a same-titled Epic is a milestone container,
341	       never an FR to join;
342	     - `labels = "<repo_tag>"` when `### Jira`.repo_tag is declared (a
343	       free-form sub-section field, parsed like `default_labels`);
344	     - `summary ~ "\"<title>\""` — the quoted-phrase form. Without the
345	       escaped inner quotes `~` widens from a phrase match to a word match.
346	
347	     **The query narrows the page; the client decides the join.** `~` is a
348	     text match, never an identity test, so a non-empty page is NOT a hit.
349	     `decide` compares each candidate's summary against `title` under the
350	     ONE normalizer, `normalizeTitleForCompare` (trim, collapse ASCII space
351	     runs, fold en/em dashes and NBSP, drop a heading anchor), and joins
352	     only on that — never re-derive the compare by hand. This is the shape § Milestone Listing already ships twice:
353	     broad JQL then a client-side name filter (Epic leg), broad
354	     `labels IS NOT EMPTY` then a client-side exact-anchored label match
355	     (label leg). The binding path further down already concedes the
356	     principle — "For an Epic-KEYED milestone, summary equality is not the
357	     join" — the create path simply never inherited it.
358	
359	     **A page that reaches the cap is uncertainty, not a miss.** Mirror the
360	     milestone listing's `MILESTONE_PAGE_CAP` treatment: if the last page
361	     still reports `isLast: false`, the ticket has NOT been proven absent. Do not create on it — surface
362	     `tracker_idempotency_uncertain` and let the operator decide.
363	   - **A candidate that fails a conjunct the query carried refuses the
364	     page.** A tracker that honours its own filter never returns another
365	     repository's differently-tagged ticket, an Epic, or a ticket outside the
366	     container, so one on the page means the page came from some other
367	     search. `decide` refuses it as `page-violates-query` with
368	     `tracker_idempotency_uncertain`: re-run the search `query` printed, and
369	     never join or create beside it.
370	   - `mcp__atlassian__createJiraIssue(projectKey=<from CLAUDE.md ### Jira>, summary=title, description=<rendered template>, issuetype=<resolved type>, contentFormat: "markdown")`,
371	     carrying the `createPayload`'s `labels` and, when present, its `parent`
372	     — so the new ticket lands already inside its milestone container and a
373	     retry's narrowed query can find it. Create only on a `create` decision.
374	   - **Network-error retry path (Gateway-Timeout idempotency hardening).**
375	     If the create call returns a network-error response
376	     (Gateway-Timeout / 504 / connection reset / equivalent) instead of a
377	     successful key, the server-side write may have landed despite the
378	     timeout (smoke #6 finding F6: the original write succeeded as `DST-2`
379	     while the timeout caused the retry path to fire). Re-run the JQL
380	     idempotency probe with backoff to give Atlassian's eventual-consistency
381	     window time to settle:
382	
383	     | Attempt | Wait before probe | Action |
384	     |---------|-------------------|--------|
385	     | 1       | 1 second          | The narrowed JQL probe (container conjunct + repo tag + `summary ~` phrase), then the client-side normalized compare |
386	     | 2       | 2 seconds         | Same narrowed JQL probe, same client-side compare |
387	     | 3       | 4 seconds         | Same narrowed JQL probe, same client-side compare |
388	
389	
390	     **Every retry attempt runs the same four steps.** For attempt `N` of
391	     three (`retry-1`, `retry-2`, `retry-3`), after that attempt's wait:
392	
393	     1. `bun run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/adapters/_shared/src/create_idempotency_probe.ts query <projectRoot> --title <title> [container]`;
394	     2. `mcp__atlassian__searchJiraIssuesUsingJql` with the printed `jql` and `fields`;
395	     3. save the page(s), then
396	        `bun run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/adapters/_shared/src/create_idempotency_probe.ts decide <projectRoot> <page.json>... --title <title> [container] --attempt retry-<N>`;
397	     4. act on `outcome`: `reused` → return `key`; `miss` (attempts 1-2
398	        only) → wait and run the next attempt; `refused` → stop with
399	        `tracker_idempotency_uncertain`; `create` (attempt 3 only, no
400	        `repo_tag` declared) → one `mcp__atlassian__createJiraIssue` from
401	        the printed `createPayload`, plus the warning row below.
402	
403	     In a shared repository a create decision authorises one create call:
404	     a create that times out again goes back through `decide`, never
405	     straight to a second create.
406	
407	     Three attempts total; the schedule is `1s + 2s + 4s` (cumulative ~7s

494	## Project Milestone — milestone-as-Epic via `parent`, label fallback
495	
496	Jira opts into project-milestone binding (`project_milestone: true` in the
497	frontmatter). Jira has no per-issue "milestone" field on the standard MCP
498	surface, but it does have a native container: the **Epic**. The primary
499	binding (`milestone_binding: epic` in the frontmatter) realises each
500	milestone as an Epic issue created under its human title, from whose
501	tracker-assigned key the milestone id is derived; the
502	FR Task binds by pointing its `parent` field at that Epic's key. When the
503	bound project has no Epic type (or cannot set `parent`), the binding
504	degrades to the legacy **label** path documented further down — never a
505	hard failure.
506	
507	### Epic path (primary — `milestone_binding: epic`)
508	
509	**Find.** Enumerate the project's Epics via
510	`mcp__atlassian__searchJiraIssuesUsingJql` with
511	`jql = "project = <projectKey> AND issuetype = Epic"` and match the milestone's
512	Epic by KEY when the plan heading carries an `M_<key>` token: sanitize each
513	candidate's key forward (`GF-78` → `M_GF_78`) and compare. For an Epic-KEYED
514	milestone, summary equality is not the join — the canonical name embeds the
515	very key being looked for, while the Epic itself carries the human title typed
516	at creation. A name that carries NO token — a pre-key human title, the state
517	between minting the Epic and writing the plan file — has no key to compare, so
518	that one arm still matches by NAME, byte-exactly. Both arms refuse on a miss:
519	binding never creates.
520	
521	**Mint — create, read the key back, derive the id, then write the plan file.**
522	A milestone Epic is minted in the only order whose values exist at the moment
523	each is needed. `adapters/_shared/src/mint_milestone_epic.ts` performs steps
524	1–3; its caller performs step 4. Step 1 is wrapped in a find-before-create
525	retry on the canonical `1s + 2s + 4s` schedule: a create that lands in Jira and
526	then times out is FOUND on the retry and reused, never created a second time.
527	That protection is why a timeout does not mint a duplicate Epic.
528	
529	1. Create the Epic with the **human title alone** —
530	   `mcp__atlassian__createJiraIssue(projectKey=<projectKey>,
531	   issueTypeName="Epic", summary=<human title>)`. The canonical
532	   `M_<key> — <Title>` name is not available here: it embeds the key Jira is
533	   about to allocate for this very Epic, so ordering it would order a value
534	   that does not yet exist.
535	2. **read the key back** from the create response, verbatim (`GF-78`).
536	3. **derive the id** from that key via `milestoneIdFromEpicKey` (`GF-78` →
537	   `M_GF_78`); a key that will not sanitize into a well-formed id refuses
538	   rather than yielding a malformed one.
539	4. **write the plan file** under that id, with heading `## M_<key> — <Title>`.
540	
541	**Epic label — at mint time only.** After it derives the id, and outside the
542	step-1 retry, the mint writes the label `milestone-M_<key>` on the Epic itself
543	(`milestone-M_GF_78` for `GF-78`). That label is a read-side convenience: it
544	lets a repo enumerating a shared project find the milestone by its label. It
545	is never the binding surface — membership stays the FR's `parent`, below. A
546	failed label write never fails the mint: the Epic and its derived id stand,
547	and only the convenience is missing. In a live session the write is a
548	read-merge-write on the Epic's own key —
549	`mcp__atlassian__editJiraIssue(issueIdOrKey=<epic-key>,
550	additional_fields={ labels: [...<existing labels>, "milestone-M_<key>"] })`,
551	never clobbering a label already there. `mintMilestoneEpic` performs it
552	through the provider's `addLabel` and reports whether it landed as
553	`labelled`; its command form prints the label it would write as
554	`label=milestone-M_<key>` beside the derived id.
555	
556	**Joining, never minting.** A repo joining a container another repo already
557	minted calls the mint with `{ join: true }`. Its find leg compares titles
558	after normalizing whitespace and case: exactly one match joins that Epic, two
559	or more refuse and name every candidate with its key, and no match — or a
560	provider carrying no `listEpics` — refuses instead of creating. A join never
561	creates. The toolkit makes every other mint with the approved decision of
562	`resolve_milestone_identity.ts` as `expect`, so it performs that act or refuses; only a bare mint with neither option still finds by title.
563	
564	The mint surfaces NO capability row: it is a step of its own, not an attach
565	outcome, and the attach that follows FINDS the Epic and returns `capability:
566	null`. `milestone_create_required` belongs to the object binding's
567	`save_milestone` auto-create, which this path never reaches.
568	
569	**Membership — `parent` set.** Bind the FR Task by writing the Epic's key to
570	its `parent` field: `mcp__atlassian__editJiraIssue(issueIdOrKey=ticket_id,
571	additional_fields={ parent: { key: <epic-key> } })`. This path never touches
572	milestone objects. For an Epic-KEYED milestone the per-FR attach writes no
573	`milestone-<M-token>` label on the FR ticket; the only `milestone-M_<key>`
574	label such a milestone carries is the one the mint writes on the Epic itself.
575	A grandfathered NUMERIC `M<N>` milestone under this same binding deliberately
576	DOES take the label surface on the ticket, because that is where the reader's
577	own grandfather clause looks for it; see the numeric note below.
578	Idempotency pre-check: the issue is read FIRST, before any Epic is listed
579	(STE-611). When its binding is already present the attach is a no-op, with
580	no enumeration and no write, even when that parent Epic lives in another
581	project (a legacy `GB-40` parent under a repository now bound to `GF`).
582	
583	**Read-back verify.** Re-read the issue (`getJiraIssue`) and assert
584	`parent = <epic-key>`. A mismatch surfaces the canonical binding-mismatch
585	error (never retried); transient failures retry the whole round-trip on the
586	canonical `1s + 2s + 4s` schedule.
587	
588	**Grandfathered numeric milestones — the numeric note.** A project that adopts
589	Epic-keyed milestones still has its old numeric `M<N>` ones. Under this same
590	`milestone_binding: epic`, a numeric token does NOT bind by parent Epic: it
591	takes the `milestone-M<N>` LABEL surface, through the same read-merge-write
592	attach the legacy binding uses. That is not an inconsistency — it is the only
593	arrangement that converges, because the reader's own grandfather clause looks
594	for a numeric milestone on the label surface. Binding by parent while the
595	reader checks labels is what made a backfill sweep report the same work done on
596	every pass forever. There is nothing to configure: the routing is decided by
597	the milestone TOKEN's kind, not by the adapter's declared binding.
598	
599	**Epic-absent fallback.** Probe the bound project's issue-type metadata via
600	`mcp__atlassian__getJiraProjectIssueTypesMetadata`. When the Epic type is
601	absent — or the project cannot set `parent` — the attach degrades to the
602	label path below and the closing summary surfaces the **informational**
603	`milestone_epic_unsupported` capability row (the FR still attaches via the
604	legacy label; the degraded path is never an error).
605	
606	### Label path (fallback — legacy `milestone_binding: label`)
607	
608	Each FR's frontmatter `milestone: M<N>` maps to the
609	`milestone-<M-token>` label (e.g. `milestone-M86`), and the milestone-attach
610	flow (`/spec-write` § 0b, `/implement` Phase 1 step 0.e) attaches that label
611	to the pushed ticket.
612	
613	**Mapping.** FR `milestone: M<N>` → the `milestone-<M-token>` label. The
614	token is the raw milestone token (`M86`), giving labels like
615	`milestone-M86`. The label is created implicitly the first time it is
616	attached — there is no pre-existing tracker milestone object to look up
617	(this is the `N/A (create-on-write)` missing-milestone handling from
618	`docs/tracker-adapters.md`).
619	
620	**Attach — `editJiraIssue` read-merge-write.** Jira's MCP has no top-level
621	`labels` parameter on the edit path and no append-a-label operation; a
622	naive write would clobber every other label on the issue. So the attach is
623	a **read-merge-write** cycle:
624	
625	1. **Read** — `mcp__atlassian__getJiraIssue(issueIdOrKey=ticket_id)` and
626	   capture the issue's current `labels` array.
627	2. **Merge** — union the existing labels with `milestone-<M-token>`; if the
628	   label is already present this is a no-op set (idempotent).
629	3. **Write** — `mcp__atlassian__editJiraIssue(issueIdOrKey=ticket_id,
630	   additional_fields={ labels: <merged set> })` with the full merged array,
631	   so no pre-existing label is dropped. (There is no top-level `labels`
632	   parameter — labels go through `additional_fields.labels`, the same path
633	   the on-create `default_labels` rule uses; see the MCP tool-names table.)
634	
635	**Read-back verify.** After the write, **re-read** the issue
636	(`getJiraIssue`) and assert the `milestone-<M-token>` label is present in
637	the returned `labels` — the read-back verify confirms the attach landed
638	(the same silent-no-op discipline the metadata writes use). If the label is
639	absent on read-back, surface an NFR-10 canonical-shape warning rather than
640	reporting success.
641	
642	**`default_labels` carve-out (on-create only).** The `### Jira`.default_labels
643	workspace-binding field applies **only on create** (`createJiraIssue`),
644	per the workspace-binding rule documented under `upsert_ticket_metadata`.
645	The milestone-attach read-merge-write runs on the **edit** path and is
646	entirely independent of `default_labels`: it neither reads nor reapplies
647	`default_labels`, and attaching a milestone label never re-triggers the
648	create-time default-labels behaviour. Conversely, a create that seeds
649	`default_labels` does not attach the milestone label — milestone binding is
650	always its own explicit read-merge-write step.
651	
652	## Milestone Listing — `listMilestones()` via Epic enumeration + grandfathered labels
653	
654	The Jira `AdapterDriver` implements the optional `listMilestones()` method so
655	the tracker leg of `nextFreeMilestoneNumber` fires in Jira mode. With the
656	Epic-first binding (§ Project Milestone above), *listing* milestones means
657	*enumerating milestone Epics* — a handful of objects, never a full
658	labelled-task scan — with the legacy `milestone-<M-token>` labels unioned in
659	as a grandfathered second leg so pre-Epic milestones stay visible. That leg
660	is no longer legacy-only: it is also the only route that sees a freshly
661	minted Epic, which carries the `milestone-M_<key>` label the mint writes but
662	not yet a summary that leads with a milestone token.
663	
664	**Pure-function core.** The two-leg scan + pagination + dedupe logic lives in
665	the Schema-P helper `adapters/jira/src/list_milestones.ts`
666	(`listMilestones(fetchPage, opts?)`; the Epic leg injects via
667	`opts.fetchEpicPage`), mirroring `discover_field.ts`: no network in the
668	function itself — the caller injects the fetchers, which wrap the MCP calls.
669	`TrackerProvider.listMilestones()` already delegates
670	`driver.listMilestones?.() ?? []`, so no provider change is needed; the Jira
671	driver simply supplies this method.
672	
673	**Procedure (driver wiring).**
674	
675	1. **Epic leg (primary)** — `mcp__atlassian__searchJiraIssuesUsingJql` with
676	   `jql = "project = <projectKey> AND issuetype = Epic ORDER BY created DESC"`
677	   (project key from `### Jira`.project), paginating page by page. Feed each
678	   raw search answer, verbatim — plain or wrapped — into the helper's `fetchEpicPage`.
679	   Client-side name filter: an Epic counts iff its summary's first
680	   whitespace-delimited word is a valid milestone token (union grammar); each
681	   match contributes `M_<epic-key>` (key verbatim).
682	2. **Label leg (grandfathered labels and freshly minted Epics)** — the same JQL tool with
683	   `jql = "project = <projectKey> AND labels IS NOT EMPTY ORDER BY created DESC"`,
684	   feeding each raw search answer, verbatim, into `fetchPage`.
685	   This JQL deliberately carries no `issuetype` filter, and that absence is
686	   what lets the label leg return an Epic carrying the `milestone-M_<epic-key>`
687	   label the mint writes — so a repo joining a shared project finds a freshly
688	   minted Epic even before its summary is renamed to lead with a milestone
689	   token (the only thing the Epic leg in step 1 counts); adding an `issuetype`
690	   filter to this JQL would hide those Epics.
691	   Client-side, each label is matched against the exact-anchored union shape
692	   `^milestone-(<M-token>)$` — accepting `milestone-M<N>` and
693	   `milestone-M_<epic-key>` while `milestone-foo`, `milestone-`,
694	   `xmilestone-M5`, `M5`, `milestone-M5-extra`, `milestone-M5 ` all stay
695	   rejected, matching the create-on-write `milestone-<M-token>` derivation.
696	3. **Return** — the deduped union of both legs as bare tokens
697	   (`{ name }[]` of `M<N>` / `M_<epic-key>` — **not** the `milestone-`
698	   label), numeric tokens first ascending, epic-keyed tokens after (opaque,
699	   code-point order) — so the existing `scanTracker` extractor in
700	   `next_free_milestone_number.ts` consumes it unchanged and `M_<key>` ids
701	   never bump the sequential counter.
702	
703	**Pagination cap, no silent truncation.** Each leg paginates to a documented
704	cap (`MILESTONE_PAGE_CAP`, default 50; overridable via `opts.pageCap`). If the
705	cap is reached before a page proves it is the last (plain `isLast`, or wrapped
706	`issues.pageInfo.hasNextPage: false`), the helper stops that leg and
707	surfaces a one-line log (`opts.log`) noting pages may have been dropped —
708	never a silent truncation.
709	
710	**Fail-soft / non-load-bearing.** Any JQL / network failure — including a
711	failure on a later page of either leg — degrades `listMilestones()` to `[]`;
712	it never throws into allocation. Identical posture to Linear's milestone leg
713	and the cross-branch git leg.
714	
715	> **Supersedes.** The Epic leg supersedes the label-only listing that closed
716	> the deferred *listing* half of the create-on-write `milestone-<M-token>`
717	> label binding (itself superseding the never-shipped "Jira milestone API"
718	> enumeration). Grandfathered labels remain listed via the union so pre-Epic
719	> milestones never disappear; attach (write) and listing (read) stay
720	> orthogonal halves of the same milestone model. (Ticket-level traceability
721	> lives in the FR + git history, not in this shipped adapter doc.)
